title: My Knee Hurts
can_do: 说出轻微不适的位置和感觉，让成人立即停止活动并提供照护。
trigger: During ordinary quiet play, he lightly bumps his right knee on the low table and tells Mom it hurts.
repair_response: Not my thumb. This finger hurts.
setting: At home just after a small knee bump during quiet play beside the sofa.

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: We're stopping now. Let me look.

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: Would you like a cold cloth?

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: I'll hold it gently on your knee.

replay_cards.title: A sore finger
replay_cards.change: He gently bumps one finger and stops building
replay_cards.challenge: Tell Mom it hurts; Mom immediately stops and checks. If she looks toward the thumb, clarify 'Not my thumb. This finger hurts.' Point to the affected finger and accept appropriate help without demonstrating the bump again.

replay_cards.title: An itchy sleeve
replay_cards.change: His shirt sleeve feels itchy against his arm
replay_cards.challenge: Name the arm and the itchy feeling. Dad pauses dressing immediately, checks the sleeve, and helps him choose another comfortable shirt. He reports whether the change helps; he is not told the cause or required to tolerate it.

parent_support: Stop and attend to the first pain signal before asking for location or feeling details. Accept a point, a few words, or his home language; care is never conditional on further speech.
Keep the pretend bump mild and non-graphic: a small wince and a slightly quieter voice. Do not create a real bump or ask him to repeat a painful movement.

Acknowledge the report calmly, check without diagnosing, and offer a clean cold cloth with his agreement. Use normal caregiver judgment about any further help; the scene ends with supported rest, not a claim that the pain has disappeared.
